PASTE-READY LATEX (labels prefixed audit-ro):

\begin{remark}[\Cref{def:readout} and \Cref{lem:readout}(b): the pinning needs no dyadicity, and has none]\label{rem:audit-ro-nondyadic}
Two repairs to \Cref{def:readout}. First, \Cref{lem:gadget} produces the
values $1-2^{-m}$ only; a chain of value an arbitrary dyadic $y_v$ is
\Cref{lem:dyadic-row} with the single target $t_1$ and $r_1=y_v$, at most
$d$ average vertices when $y_v$ has denominator $2^{d}$. Second, and better,
no chain and no dyadicity are needed: let $G[y]$ be $G$ with each $x_v$
\emph{retyped as a terminal of payoff $y_v$}, which \Cref{rem:terminals}
licenses for arbitrary constant payoffs in $[0,1]$, carrying
\Cref{thm:contraction}, \Cref{thm:stopping-determinacy} and
\Cref{cor:comparison} unchanged. With that reading
\Cref{lem:readout}(a),(b),(c) hold verbatim for every $y\in[0,1]^{m}$ and
the parenthesis ``which is dyadic (\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp})'' in (b)
must be deleted: it is false, and \Cref{lem:denominator-sharp} does not
assert it, bounding the denominator only by \emph{an integer} at most
$2^{a}$. Indeed take $\Vmax=\{x\}$, $\Vavg=\{g_1,g_2\}$ and
\[
  x\to\{g_1,t_0\},\qquad g_1\to\{t_1,g_2\},\qquad g_2\to\{x,t_0\}.
\]
Each of $g_1,g_2$ has a sink successor, so by \Cref{lem:trapchar} the only
trap is empty and $G$ is stopping; the first-passage row of $x$'s first
action is the dyadic substochastic row $\tfrac14\to x$, $\tfrac12\to t_1$.
For $\sigma(x)=g_1$ one computes $\val_\sigma=(\tfrac23,\tfrac23,\tfrac13)$
at $(x,g_1,g_2)$, so $x_\sigma=(\tfrac23)$ is not dyadic, while
$\tfrac23\ne0=\val_\sigma(t_0)$ makes $G$ nondegenerate. This is the
phenomenon already recorded in \Cref{rem:alphabet-down}: values need not be
dyadic.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The grid of \Cref{rem:grid-per-vertex}]\label{rem:audit-ro-grid}
The values of a stopping SSG do not lie on the grid of mesh $2^{-a}$. By
\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp} they lie in the Farey set
$\mathcal F_a:=\{p/q:0\le p\le q\le2^{a}\}\cap[0,1]$, of size
$D(a)=1+\sum_{q\le2^{a}}\varphi(q)=\Theta(4^{a})$: $2,3,7,23,81,325,1261$
for $a=0,\dots,6$, against $2^{a}+1=2,3,5,9,17,33,65$. What
\Cref{thm:switch-count} uses is not a grid but the common denominator
\emph{inside a single value vector} (\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp} applied to
$v_{\sigma_j,\tau_j}$), so its proof and its constants stand. In
\Cref{rem:grid-per-vertex}, however, the successive values of $\val(v)$ come
from different vectors with different denominators, so the correct reading
is $L\le\sum_vn_v\le m(D(a)-1)$ with $D(a)$ the Farey count, and that is not
a constant-factor refinement of $N2^{a}$: at $a=2$ it reads $6m$ against
$4N$, weaker as soon as $m>2N/3$. The remark's two substantive claims are
untouched --- at $a=0$, $D(0)=2$ and $L\le m$, attained by $\mathrm{RC}(k)$
with $L=N-2$ (re-verified for $k\le9$).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Exhaustiveness in \Cref{lem:profile-trichotomy}]\label{rem:audit-ro-trichotomy}
``Case (b) is (a) with $\pi,\pi'$ exchanged'' proves the implication in (b),
not that the three cases exhaust; the missing case is
$\varepsilon_v(f_{v,b}(x)-x(v))<0$. Say $v\in\Vmax$. Then $T_{\pi'}x\le x$
with strict inequality at $v$, so $y\le x$ by \Cref{cor:comparison}. If also
$f_{v,a}(y)\le y(v)$ then $T_\pi y\le y$, so $x\le y$ and $y=x$; but then
$y(v)=f_{v,b}(y)=f_{v,b}(x)<x(v)=y(v)$, absurd. Hence $f_{v,a}(y)>y(v)$,
that is $v\in s_C(\pi')$, which is case (b).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Numerical corrections in \Cref{prop:m3-realised}]\label{rem:audit-ro-m3}
Re-verified from the eighteen games in exact arithmetic --- trap test,
$\val_\sigma$ as the componentwise minimum over all $2^{k}$ positional
$\tau$, outmap, ties --- the counts $728$, $18$, $16$ and the vertex numbers
$28$ to $62$, $98$ and $170$ are right and every game is stopping and
tie-free. Two corrections. The sixteen one-player games have harmonic normal
forms of denominator $64$ or $128$, not ``up to $512$''; $512$ is the
denominator of the $170$-vertex two-player realisation of the class
$(0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4)$, the $98$-vertex one having denominator $64$. And ``at
$m=3$ one-player realisability is exactly the Holt--Klee condition'' holds
among the \emph{acyclic} orientations only: the $3$-cube's nineteenth class,
the cyclic one with canonical outmap $(0,3,6,1,5,4,2,7)$, satisfies
Holt--Klee on every face, yet no game realises it, improvement orientations
being acyclic (\Cref{prop:allsw-auso}, \Cref{thm:flat-resolution}).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Witnesses for the $m\le3$ projection claim]\label{rem:audit-ro-lift}
The claim after \Cref{prop:seven-k1} is verified in full. For a Holt--Klee
USO $s$ of the $3$-cube with sink $o$, the $4$-cube orientation with layer
$0$ equal to $s$, layer $1$ the uniform orientation $v\mapsto v\oplus o$ and
every inner edge pointing into layer $0$ is a Holt--Klee USO projecting to
$s$; this was checked for all $672$ Holt--Klee USOs of the $3$-cube and
fails for exactly the $72$ non-Holt--Klee ones. For those, explicit
